title: Capacity planning and tenant resource isolation
status_rationale: No production system, load test, capacity model or performance baseline exists as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Capacity is planned from documented volume drivers (accounts per sponsor, activity segments, grant volume, document generation, AI-assisted case volume) and monitored against benchmarked sustainable capacity of the largest sponsor database; action is taken before peak commit rate reaches 50 percent of that capacity. Each sponsor has its own database by default, and quotas bound connections, API rates, fan-out and agent usage per tenant so no tenant can degrade another. When demand exceeds capacity, the system applies backpressure and queues deferrable work rather than failing, and never queues approvals or payments in a way that bypasses revalidation.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-XIN-EVA-013 sets the 50 percent threshold for introducing additional infrastructure; RR-UNB-ECO-001-r2 lists volume drivers.
intended_practice: Build the capacity model alongside the first load test.
customer_statement: No capacity plan exists because no production system exists. Our design isolates each sponsor's database by default and sets explicit capacity thresholds.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Load testing and peak-event readiness
status_rationale: No production system, load test, capacity model or performance baseline exists as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Load tests on the selected managed PostgreSQL model the year-end peak of the largest expected sponsor at ten times normal grant volume, plus historical replay and projection rebuild at production scale, and run as a release gate for high-volume paths. Year-end readiness includes a documented plan, conjunction drills (surge plus market plus provider plus regulatory change) and a staffing surge playbook. Results with thresholds and pass/fail are shared under NDA.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-IMM-010, UNB-ACC-036, UNB-WF-005 and TVR-OPS-003 require surge testing and year-end readiness; none has run.
intended_practice: Run the first surge benchmark before choosing to add any second store or broker, as UNB-XIN-EVA-013 requires.
customer_statement: No load testing has been performed. Our requirements call for testing at ten times normal grant volume before production, including year-end peak modeling.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

challenge.customer_intent: Be confident the platform will not slow down or fail during year-end giving.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Contributions or grants miss December 31 or rail cut-offs; donors lose deductions for the intended year.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Vendors usually cite autoscaling and a periodic load test. Autoscaling does not scale a single authoritative database writer, and generic load tests rarely model the real year-end shape or long ledger histories.
challenge.historical_convention: Seasonal capacity reviews and change freezes.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partly: per-sponsor databases bound the largest single workload to one sponsor's peak rather than the sum of all sponsors.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Load test as a release gate on high-volume paths.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Quarterly load test reports and live headroom metrics.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Measured thresholds tied to architectural decisions (no new infrastructure until measured need), plus per-tenant partitioning of load.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely, if benchmark evidence is shared.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If the largest sponsor's peak exceeds what one managed PostgreSQL instance can sustain after tuning.
challenge.alternative_risks: Synthetic year-end shape may not match a real sponsor's peak, especially for a sponsor migrating mid-year.
supporting_arguments: Avoids premature complexity that itself causes outages.
Bounds blast radius of one sponsor's surge.
opposing_arguments: A single-writer database has a hard ceiling that scale-out designs avoid.
No real-world peak has been observed.

title: Performance service levels and reporting
status_rationale: No production system, load test, capacity model or performance baseline exists as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Echelon publishes performance SLOs per capability (for example interactive page response and command acknowledgment at the 95th percentile on mid-range phones over constrained networks, and maximum time from approval to payment file generation), measured with real-user monitoring segmented by device and network class and by server metrics, and reports them monthly per tenant. Performance SLOs are published only after a measured baseline exists.
intended_practice: Establish baselines in a production-like environment before offering performance commitments.
customer_statement: We do not currently offer performance service levels. We plan to publish them once we have measured baselines.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Batch windows and processing deadlines
status_rationale: No production system, load test, capacity model or performance baseline exists as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Batch work (payment file generation, reconciliation, statements, year-end acknowledgments) is scheduled against rail cut-offs and business deadlines and isolated from interactive load, so batches do not cause online slowdowns. Requests approved before a published internal cut-off are included in the next rail submission, with alerts raised before a deadline is at risk. Year-end acknowledgment and statement generation are capacity-tested for full-volume completion well before donors need them for tax filing, and Folio rendering throughput is measured before Folio is relied on for statements.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-GAP-003 (operational cut-offs and close) and CNV-EXP-001 (rendering throughput tests) specify the need. Folio is a print component system without production-qualified accessible PDF output (folio@56a18e1:docs/requirements/unbound-financial-report-consumer-capability-review-2026-11-23.md).
intended_practice: Define cut-off schedules per rail with the payments component; measure document throughput in a rendering spike.
customer_statement: We have not yet defined batch windows or cut-off schedules. We plan to schedule processing against payment-rail cut-offs and to test year-end document volumes before production.
